newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders eye EU wheat refund of 10.00 to 12.50 Ecus.
newsitem.headline: Traders eye EU wheat refund of 10.00 to 12.50 Ecus.

text.p: Grain exporters on Thursday said they expected the European Union to grant a refund of 10.00 to 12.50 Ecus per tonne on soft wheat exports at this week's tender.
Last week the EU granted the export of 436,500 tonnes of soft wheat at a refund of 10.25 Ecus per tonne.
Several exporters said the Commission may decide to raise the refund to 12.50 Ecus per tonne to help ease an export licence shortage.
But others said it may also choose to hold the refund at last week's level of around 10.00 Ecus.
"If it is generous it may well go up to 12.50. But it can also remain at 10.00 Ecus," one trader said.
Based on bids this would clear the release of between 133,000 and 332,000 tonnes of wheat in France, plus any additional tonnages granted elsewhere in the European Union, they said.
In France traders bid to export 521,200 tonnes of soft wheat at refunds ranging from 8.48 to 16.39 Ecus per tonne.
Because traders did not have a detailed breakdown of the bids in other countries, they said it was difficult to estimate the tonnages that may be awarded at the auction.
"I think it may be difficult to raise the refund from last week," one exporter aid, adding volumes granted this week may not be "substantial".
Exporters said it was hard to out-guess the Commission's moves, particularly as they did not know what export target the Commission had in mind for the 1996/97 season.
Since July 1 the Commission has granted licences to export 8.1 million of soft wheat grain. Most exporters put remaining EU export prospects at between one and 1.5 million tonnes.
Earlier on Thursday an EU grain official said the EU started the season with an informal export target of 8.0 to 9.0 million and that this target appeared easily achievable.
